topic.topicDisplayName: Musculoskeletal ultrasound in rheumatology: synovitis, power Doppler, guided injection
topic.coverageNote: The 2017 EULAR ultrasound-procedure paper was not available as full text. These two open papers cover the missing pieces: the OMERACT/EULAR ultrasound definitions of effusion, synovial hypertrophy, and Doppler signal, and the practical conduct of an ultrasound-guided musculoskeletal injection.

mcqs.question: How does the synovitis review define an effusion?

options.A: Displaceable, compressible, hypoechoic or anechoic intra-articular material that does not show a Doppler signal
options.B: Non-displaceable hyperechoic tissue with Doppler flow
options.C: Any bright line on the bone surface
options.D: A compressible mass outside the joint

mcqs.explanation: The review, citing the OMERACT/EULAR ultrasound task force, defines effusion as abnormal hypoechoic or anechoic intra-articular material that is displaceable and compressible and does not exhibit a Doppler signal.

sourceRefs.excerpt: effusion is defined as the abnormal presence of hypoechoic or anechoic intra-articular material that is displaceable and compressible, but does not exhibit a Doppler signal,

mcqs.question: How is synovial hypertrophy distinguished in that definition?

options.A: Abnormal hyperechoic intra-articular tissue that is not displaceable, is poorly compressible, and may show Doppler signal
options.B: Fluid that compresses away and has no Doppler signal

mcqs.explanation: Synovial hypertrophy is abnormal hyperechoic intra-articular tissue that is non-displaceable and poorly compressible and might exhibit a Doppler signal.

sourceRefs.excerpt: synovial hypertrophy or proliferation is represented by the abnormal presence of hyperechoic intra-articular tissue that is nondisplaceable and poorly compressible, and might also exhibit a Doppler signal.

mcqs.question: What does the review call the main ultrasound marker of inflammatory activity?

options.A: Colour or power Doppler signal within synovial hypertrophy

mcqs.explanation: The review says colour or power Doppler signal within synovial hypertrophy is the main pathologic marker of inflammatory activity.

sourceRefs.excerpt: color or power Doppler signals within synovial hypertrophy is the main pathologic marker of inflammatory activity ( , ).

mcqs.question: What combination does the procedure review say is used for the most common injections?

options.A: Local anaesthetic plus a particulate or water-soluble steroid

mcqs.explanation: The most common injections use a combination of local anaesthetic and either a particulate or water-soluble steroid for pain or swelling in a joint, bursa, tendon sheath, or nerve.

sourceRefs.excerpt: The most common injections are performed using a combination of local anesthetic and either a particulate or water-soluble steroid preparation to address symptoms of pain or swelling, usually localized to a joint (arthritis), bursa (bursitis), tendon sheath (tenosynovitis or tendinosis), or nerve (neuritis/neuroma).

mcqs.question: What does the in-plane, or long-axis, approach keep in view?

options.A: The length and tip of the needle
options.C: The needle hub, with the tip deliberately out of the image

mcqs.explanation: In the long-axis or in-plane approach the needle is seen along its length, and the length and tip are kept in view.

sourceRefs.excerpt: long axis” or “in-plane” injection approach, the transducer is orientated such that the needle will be visualized along its length, with the length and tip of the needle kept in view at all times ( ).
